# Chapter 3: Bounded Sequences

### Narrative

Chapter 2 handled monotone sequences via MCT — completeness guarantees convergence when terms march steadily toward a target. But what about bounded sequences with no monotone structure? What does completeness force on *all* bounded sequences?

This chapter answers that question. Bolzano-Weierstrass says every bounded sequence has a convergent subsequence — you can always find order hiding in the chaos. Limsup and liminf capture the "spread" of subsequential limits. The Cauchy criterion gives an intrinsic test for convergence that doesn't require knowing the limit in advance.

The chapter culminates with a revelation: these are all equivalent faces of completeness. LUB, MCT, nested intervals, Bolzano-Weierstrass, Cauchy — any one implies all the others. Completeness is a single deep property wearing many masks.
